subject: ICT
title: Left... Right...
subtitle: Find your left and right hands
hero_picture: Two Kerala children riding on a friendly elephant's back at a crossroads, one pointing left and the other pointing right, a cat watching.

sections.heading: Help the elephant
text: Kannan and Meenu are riding an elephant.
'To the left!' says one. 'To the right!' says the other.
Which way should the elephant go?
sections.caption: Which way to go?
sections.picture: An elephant with two children on its back at a fork in a jungle path, one child pointing left, one pointing right.

sections.heading: My two hands
text: One is my left hand. One is my right hand.
Most of us write with the right hand.
sections.caption: Left hand and right hand
sections.picture: A child holding up both hands with palms facing out: a red band on the left wrist and a blue band on the right wrist.

sections.heading: The hand game
text: Open 'Find your left and right hands'.
A hand is shown on the screen.
Is it a left hand or a right hand?
sections.caption: A hand on the screen
sections.picture: A laptop screen showing a picture of one open hand and two plain buttons below it.

sections.heading: Check with your hands
text: Match them with the hand on the screen.
Then click the right button below.
sections.caption: Matching hands
sections.picture: A child at a laptop looking at their own hands to decide, comparing with the hand on the screen.

sections.heading: Left, right game
text: 'Turn right!' Now turn to the right.
sections.caption: Turning left and right
sections.picture: Children in a playground playing a game, all turning to their left together on a teacher's call.

rhyme: Left hand up, right hand too,
Turn to the left, turn to the right,
Now I know them, day and night!
activity: Stand in front of a mirror. Raise your right hand. Which hand does the mirror boy or girl raise?
talk: Which hand do you write with?
What do we click after finding the hand?
summary: We have a left hand and a right hand; we can find which is which.

questions.prompt: How many hands do we have?
questions.explanation: We have a left hand and a right hand.

questions.prompt: In the game, what is shown on the screen?
What do we do after finding the hand?

questions.explanation: Most children write with the right hand.
